title: routing-result
description: One normalized backend execution outcome (#248, increment A of #109). failure_class is CAUSE — never provider wording, never routing action; increment B owns the mapping from class to routing behavior, and `unknown` fails closed: no retry or failover semantics may attach to it by default. VERSIONING NOTE (#109 increment F): the four context_limit_* fields are additive and are intentionally NOT in `required`. Marking them required would invalidate every version-1 record written before F, and forking to version 2 would split the contract for a purely additive group. Legacy records therefore remain valid without them, while NEWLY PRODUCED records are held to the full group — presence and internal consistency — by rr_doc_invariant in scripts/lib/routing-result.sh, which is the runtime normalization boundary every new document passes through. Read the two together: this file is the compatibility contract, rr_doc_invariant is the production contract.

failure_class.description: null exactly when outcome is success. quota_exhausted (a shared allowance is spent — hours-scale, pool-scoped) is NOT rate_limited (short-horizon throttling); execution is a task failure, never a provider event; auth and invalid_request never read as 'try another profile'; denied is a policy refusal that is never rerouted around.

effective_model.description: The model that actually served the request, when verifiable; null when it cannot be verified — NEVER silently assumed equal to requested_model.

reset_at.description: Provider-supplied reset time (ISO-8601) when present in the evidence; null otherwise.

upstream_origin.description: The sanitized CONFIGURED launch origin (scheme/host/port, never credentials or paths) — the host this attempt was DIRECTED at; null when unknown. NOT evidence about the host that answered: where the configured URL is a gateway, this is the gateway. See effective_upstream for the observed fact.

upstream_origin_source.description: How CCT learned upstream_origin (#273 T2/T3, FR-E8). CLOSED and semantically specific rather than a vague `configured`, so an audit can tell a codex provider entry from a resolved environment variable without reading code. `backend_default` is used ONLY where the default can actually be established — otherwise `none`, because an assumed default is an assumption. Additive and NOT in `required`, on the same compatibility rule as the other additive groups.

effective_upstream.description: The OBSERVED upstream, kept strictly separate from the configured one (#273 T2, FR-E7/E9). A CLOSED TWO-STATE MACHINE: exactly {status:unverifiable, origin:null, evidence:none} — every path that exists today, since CCT shells out to CLI binaries and never sees the HTTP layer — or {status:verified, origin:<sanitized>, evidence:provider_reported}. Every other combination is refused by rr_upstream_invariant at the runtime boundary; JSON Schema cannot express the cross-field rule, so this file states it and that predicate enforces it. `origin` is typed string-or-null rather than always-null deliberately: encoding today's incompleteness as a permanent type would force this contract to change the day a provider-reported signal appears, instead of being populated by it.

origin.description: Non-null ONLY in the verified state, and then sanitized by the same origin-only rules as upstream_origin. A provider-reported value is authoritative about identity, never trusted as safe text.

status.description: verified: an authoritative provider-reported upstream was observed. unverifiable: nothing authoritative was learned — a configured origin, a gateway, a proxy or a backend default can NEVER produce `verified`.

evidence.description: provider_reported exactly in the verified state; none otherwise.

context_limit_declared.description: The operator-declared context window for this profile, in tokens (registry `context_limit`); null when undeclared. Undeclared NEVER means unlimited.

context_limit_observed.description: An explicit numeric server maximum read from this attempt's own overflow evidence; null when the failure stated no number, or was not a context overflow. This is an UPPER BOUND seen while FAILING — it proves the ceiling is at most this value, never that this value works.

context_limit_effective.description: min(declared, observed) — the limit selection enforces. Null whenever context_limit_declared is null, EVEN IF something was observed: an upper bound has nothing to narrow and never substitutes for a declaration (#109 increment F, FR-F6).

context_limit_evidence.description: Source of context_limit_observed; null exactly when context_limit_observed is null.

usage.description: Routed usage/cost evidence (#273, increment G of #109 — acceptance criterion C30). Additive and NOT in `required`, on the same compatibility rule as the context_limit_* group: pre-G records stay valid, while newly produced records are held to the full block by ru_doc_invariant at the runtime boundary. THE GOVERNING RULE: unknown stays unknown — no token count is invented, and no USD is claimed because a cost cap or estimate exists.

status.description: `reported` when the backend exposed at least one token count; `unavailable` when it exposes no token accounting at all. `unavailable` carries null for every value — never a zero-fill, which would be a false claim of zero usage.

usd.description: null whenever the basis is unpriced or unavailable. NEVER 0 for unknown — zero means a genuine zero.

basis.description: reported: the backend stated a USD figure for this attempt. computed: derived from observed tokens and the configured price table. unpriced: the model is known but has no price entry. unavailable: nothing to price — no tokens and no reported cost, which is also the honest answer for subscription execution where a per-request marginal cost is not attributable.

price_version.description: The rate's effective_date. Non-null exactly for `computed`; may be non-null for `reported` when the backend supplies one.
